program: Sexual assault counseling, advocacy and prevention education

what: ZCenter provides free, confidential support to sexual assault survivors and their families in Lake and northern Cook counties.
Its services include counseling in English and Spanish, a support line and referrals.
Advocacy and prevention education complement counseling at its Gurnee location, while Skokie currently provides counseling only.
strengths: Free bilingual services reduce barriers to specialist support.
Individual and group counseling offer a plausible route to short-term trauma recovery.
Local referrals and advocacy can help survivors navigate additional needs.
reservations: The reported 447 counseled conflicts with adult 384 plus child 213, so unique throughput remains uncertain.
Adult trials do not establish local QALYs, child effects or durable earnings.
Household net gains, volunteer opportunity costs and marginal donor response are unmeasured.

sections.what: Zacharias Sexual Abuse Center, EIN 36-3314976, provides free individual and group counseling to adults and children, a confidential English/Spanish support line and referrals. Gurnee in Lake County also provides advocacy and outreach; Skokie in Cook County currently provides counseling only. Both locations fall within the Chicago metro boundary. The official giving page identifies the independent recipient, but no donation transaction was tested. [Services](https://zcenter.org/survivor-services/services/)
sections.monitoring: The fiscal 2025 Year in Review covers July 2024–June 2025. Its first page reports 447 counseled, 384 adults and 213 children, whose sum is 597. We use 384 as a reported category only, with a judged uniqueness share of 0.8, not confirmed unique or completed therapy. Calls, advocacy clients and students may overlap and are not added. The CEO describes a lower waiting list without establishing marginal funding need. Obtain reconciled unique adults, treatment dose, symptom outcomes and household resource burdens before treating this as calibrated EV.
sections.qualitative: Free bilingual counseling offers a plausible trauma-recovery mechanism. Cochrane supports low-certainty short-term adult symptom improvement across heterogeneous interventions; high attrition and limited harms reporting weaken local transfer. No QALY conversion or durable recipient effect was measured. Child counseling, advocacy and prevention are outside this narrow priced channel, with their benefits and burdens unknown. Public funding and alternative free providers remain the counterfactual.
sections.cost: The conditional center is $16.855 million per ten combined equivalents: 1.37222 clinical QALYs plus 0.12319 signed household-resource equivalents. Cost is full annual economic recognized resources: $2,454,250 Form 990 expense + $61,260 netted event costs + $5,000 Schedule D donated services = $2,520,510. Against this full denominator, adult category 384 × judged uniqueness 0.8 × annual-work response 0.5 gives 153.6 exposed household units, with one welfare-equivalent person per unit. Clinical completion 0.6, utility 0.03 and duration 0.5 year after 0.25-year delay are unsupported conditional priors, not measured local effect. Independent resource success 0.2 gives 30.72 households a hypothetical finite one-year $1,500 net access/work gain after taxes, benefits, replacement earnings and new costs; retain half for positive overlap then subtract full $100 participation burden, leaving $650. The other 122.88 households lose $100. One joint log per household is counted, with no retail counseling price or ordinary survivor wages. Clinical null retains all resource costs. Harm applies to the full exposed union; clinical recipients are its subset. Central external/provider/payer losses are unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world incidence. Matched payer and volunteer-resource stresses retain full losses. Gain exposure is at most one year; zero resource duration removes all signed gains but not attendance burden. Longer clinical durations are discounted year by year, including negative symptoms; union harm is charged once.
sections.funding: Gross comparable FY2023–2025 recognized costs are $1,900,276, $2,156,058 and $2,520,510; mean $2,192,281.33. Schedule D omitted donated services and netted event costs are added once. The FY2024 audit independently confirms prior gross functional totals and notes substantial unrecognized volunteer services. Its $7,069,345 net assets include property and restrictions, not all spendable cash. FY2025 government grants $1,236,493 imply potential funding replacement. Annual response 0.5 is a conditional annual-work counterfactual, not measured next-gift capacity or a separate donor haircut. Donation website and recipient are verified; no checkout transaction was completed.

model.costScope: Conditional narrow adult counseling channel against whole annual cost; not complete recipient EV or marginal gift efficiency.
model.geographicAttribution: Lake and Cook county adult counseling household opportunities; all modeled local. Other programs unpriced.
model.formula: exposed=N*unique*b; clinical=positiveOnly(exposed*completion*q,clinicalOverlap)*discountedYears(T,delay,r) minus full once-only exposed*harm at delay, then geography once. Resource success share jointly nets positiveOnly(gain,overlap)*resourceYears-cost, with resourceYears in [0,1]; others=-cost. CG .5*people*discountedYears*log(1+net/householdConsumption). Matched payer losses scale resourceYears; external costs remain full.
model.counterfactual: Existing free services and publicly funded care continue; not all reported care is additional. Child, advocacy and prevention effects unknown.
model.attribution: Judged annual response beyond existing public funding and alternative providers; clinical subset of financial exposure union. Independent resource success does not depend on clinical completion.
model.uncertainty: Conditional reference, not calibrated expected value: uniqueness, completion, utility, duration, resources and donor response unmeasured.
model.nativeOutcomes: Reported adult counseling category; additional completed adult therapy, finite trauma utility and signed net household access/work resources.
